questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mkpụrụ akwụkwọ ndị e ji ede asụsụ Igbo?
questions.explanation: Chọkwa Ogbe refers to the standard Igbo alphabet, the set of letters used to write the Igbo language.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Asụsụ Igbo nwere udaume ole?
questions.explanation: Standard Igbo has eight vowel sounds, distinguished by their tongue root position, unlike languages with only five basic vowels.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nkewa udaume asatọ Igbo n'ime otu abụọ dabere na ọnọdụ ire?
options: Osuzu Udaume (Advanced Tongue Root vowel harmony split)
questions.explanation: Igbo's eight vowels are divided into two harmonising sets based on Advanced Tongue Root (ATR) position, often described as 'light' and 'heavy' vowel groups.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbochi iyi n'olu mmadụ mgbe a na-akpọ okwu, dị ka 'b', 'k', na 'm'?
questions.explanation: Consonants (mgbochiume) are speech sounds produced by obstructing airflow at some point in the vocal tract, unlike vowels.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mkpụrụokwu ndị dị ka 'm' na 'n' nwere ike ịbụ mkpụrụedemede n'onwe ha n'ụfọdụ okwu Igbo?
questions.explanation: Syllabic nasals (ndaume), such as 'm' and 'n', can function as complete syllables on their own in certain Igbo words, without needing an accompanying vowel.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ụkpụrụ nke na-eme ka udaume n'otu okwu kwekọrịta n'ọnọdụ ha (light/heavy)?
questions.explanation: Vowel harmony (ndakọrịta udaume) requires that vowels within a word generally agree in their tongue root quality (light or heavy).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ụdị asụsụ Igbo dị iche iche a na-asụ na mpaghara dị iche iche, dị ka Owerri, Onitsha, na Ohuhu?
questions.explanation: Olumba refers to the various regional dialects of Igbo spoken across different communities, as distinct from the standardised form.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ Igbo izugbe nke a na-eji akụzi n'ụlọ akwụkwọ na ndị niile na-aghọta?
questions.explanation: Igbo Izugbe (Standard Igbo) is the unified, standardised form of the language used in formal education and media, distinct from regional dialects.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mkpịsị olu dị elu n' okwu, nke a na-akpọ 'Elu' n'aka nka rịị Igbo?
questions.explanation: High tone (Elu) is one of the primary tonal levels in Igbo, distinguishing meaning between otherwise similar words.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mkpịsị olu dị ala n'okwu, nke a na-akpọ 'Ala' n'aka nka rịị Igbo?
questions.explanation: Low tone (Ala) is another primary tonal level in Igbo, working alongside high tone to distinguish word meanings.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbanwe olu nke na-eme ka olu 'Elu' dabere ma daa ala n'ihi mkpịsị olu ala gara ya aga?
questions.explanation: Downstep (mgbada) is a tonal phenomenon where a high tone is realised at a lower pitch than a preceding high tone, often due to an intervening low tone.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akara e ji egosi olu elu, ala, na mgbada n'ederede Igbo?
questions.explanation: Tone marking (aka nka rịị) refers to the diacritical marks used in writing to indicate the tonal pattern of Igbo words.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Asụsụ Igbo bụ asụsụ dị aka nka, nke pụtara na
options: asụsụ ahụ bụ nanị maka ederede
olu adịghị emetụta nsụpe okwu ma ọlị
olu dị iche iche nwere ike gbanwee nsụpe okwu
questions.explanation: As a tonal language, Igbo relies on pitch differences to distinguish between words that may share the same consonant and vowel sequence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ngalaba ọmụmụ asụsụ nke na-elebara udaasụsụ (sound system) anya?
questions.explanation: Phonology is the branch of linguistics that studies the sound system of a language, including vowels, consonants, and tone.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nkeji nke kacha nta n'ime okwu nke nwere udaume n'etiti, nke bụ ntọala mmụba okwu?
questions.explanation: A syllable is the basic unit of pronunciation, typically built around a vowel, serving as a foundational building block of spoken words.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu udaume n'ime asatọ udaume Igbo bụ nke a na-akpọ 'heavy' (osuzu ukwu)?
options: e, i, o, u naanị mgbe niile
ị, ọ, ụ, na a (dependent on the specific vowel-harmony set)
questions.explanation: Igbo's eight vowels split into two ATR-based harmony sets; the 'heavy' set typically includes vowels such as ị, ọ, and ụ, contrasting with the 'light' set.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'aka nka rịị Igbo, olu 'Ala' (Low tone) na-emetụta gịnị karịsịa n'ọdịiche okwu?
options: Ọ na-egosi ọdịiche pụtara ìhè n'echiche okwu dabere n'olu
Ọ dịghị emetụta echiche okwu ma ọ bụla
Ọ bụ naanị maka ederede egwu
questions.explanation: Low tone, like high tone, is essential in Igbo for distinguishing between words that would otherwise appear identical in spelling.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ngalaba ọmụmụ olu (tone) n'asụsụ nke na-elebara ka olu si emetụta ọdịiche okwu anya?
options: Ọmụmụ Olu Asụsụ (tonology, a branch of phonology)
questions.explanation: Tonology, a specialised branch of phonology, focuses specifically on how pitch patterns (tones) function within a language's sound system.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbochi iyi olu nke a na-akpọ site n'iji ire kpochie ikuku na mpaghara dị iche iche n'ọnụ, dị ka 'gb', 'kp'?
questions.explanation: Igbo has distinctive labial-velar consonants, such as 'gb' and 'kp', articulated with a simultaneous closure at both the lips and the back of the tongue.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe kpatara Ndaume (syllabic nasals) ji dị mkpa n'ọmụmụ udaasụsụ Igbo?
options: Ha nwere ike ịbụ mkpụrụedemede zuru oke n'onwe ha na-enweghị udaume
Ha na-apụtaghị n'ikwu okwu ma ọlị
Ha bụ naanị akara ederede na-enweghị mkpụrụ olu
questions.explanation: Syllabic nasals are notable because they can function as complete syllables by themselves, unlike ordinary consonants which require a vowel to form a syllable.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọdịiche dị n'etiti Igbo Izugbe na Olumba n'echiche ọmụmụ asụsụ?
options: Igbo Izugbe bụ ụdị asụsụ e ji akụzi n'ụlọ akwụkwọ, ebe Olumba bụ ụdị mpaghara dị iche iche
Igbo Izugbe bụ naanị olumba Onitsha
Olumba bụ naanị maka ederede egwu
Ha bụ otu ihe kpamkpam, enweghị ọdịiche ọ bụla
questions.explanation: Standard Igbo (Igbo Izugbe) is the unified form taught in schools, while dialects (olumba) reflect the natural regional variations spoken across different Igbo communities.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ụda olu nke na-adaba n'etiti Elu na Ala, na-enweghị akara pụrụ iche n'ọtụtụ ederede?
questions.explanation: Some analyses of Igbo tone recognise a mid tone level, often left unmarked in standard writing, alongside the clearly marked high and low tones.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe kpatara ọ dị mkpa ka a mata olu (tone) n'ikwu ma ọ bụ ide asụsụ Igbo nke ọma?
options: Ka echiche kwuru ghara ịgbanwe n'ihi mmezi olu adịghị mma
Olu adịghị emetụta nghọta okwu ọ bụla
Ọ bụ naanị maka egwu ọma
Ọ dịghị mkpa ma ọlị n'asụsụ Igbo
questions.explanation: Correct tone usage is essential in Igbo to avoid unintentionally changing the meaning of a word or sentence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nyocha esemokwu udaume site na nleba anya nchekwa ire n'ime ọnụ (tongue root position)?
options: Nyocha ihe ọmụmụ mmụta ọgụgụ isi
questions.explanation: ATR (Advanced Tongue Root) analysis examines the position of the tongue root during vowel articulation, which underlies Igbo's vowel harmony system.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọmụmụ nke na-eleba anya n'otu e si asụpụta mkpụrụokwu site n'ọrụ akụkụ ahụ (articulatory phonetics)?
questions.explanation: Phonetics studies the physical production of speech sounds by the vocal organs, complementing phonology's focus on how those sounds function within the language system.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu akụkụ ahịrịokwu (part of speech) nke na-akpọ aha mmadụ, ebe, ma ọ bụ ihe?
questions.explanation: A noun (mkpọha) is the part of speech used to name a person, place, or thing in Igbo grammar.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu akụkụ ahịrịokwu na-anọchi anya mkpọha n'ahịrịokwu, dị ka 'ọ', 'ha', 'anyị'?
questions.explanation: A pronoun (nnọchiaha) stands in place of a noun, such as 'he/she/it' (ọ), 'they' (ha), or 'we' (anyị).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu akụkụ ahịrịokwu na-egosi omume ma ọ bụ ihe na-eme n'ahịrịokwu, dị ka 'gaa', 'rie', 'nọdụ'?
questions.explanation: A verb (ngwaa) expresses an action or state occurring in a sentence, forming the core of the predicate.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu akụkụ ahịrịokwu na-akọwa mkpọha, dị ka 'ọma', 'ọjọọ', 'ukwu'?
questions.explanation: An adjective (ndịda) describes or modifies a noun, providing further detail about its quality.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu akụkụ ahịrịokwu na-ejikọ okwu abụọ ma ọ bụ ahịrịokwu abụọ ọnụ, dị ka 'na', 'mana', 'ma ọ bụ'?
questions.explanation: A conjunction (njikọ) joins words, phrases, or clauses together, such as 'and' (na), 'but' (mana), or 'or' (ma ọ bụ).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu akụkụ ahịrịokwu na-ejikọ mkpọha ma ọ bụ nnọchiaha na akụkụ ọzọ nke ahịrịokwu, dị ka 'na', 'n'elu'?
questions.explanation: A preposition (ibu) links a noun or pronoun to another element in the sentence, indicating relationships such as location or direction.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbanwe a na-etinye na mgbọrọgwụ ngwaa iji gosi oge ma ọ bụ ọnọdụ omume?
questions.explanation: Tense and aspect prefixes attached to verb roots indicate the timing and nature of an action, such as whether it is completed, ongoing, or habitual.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akụkụ nta kacha nta nke nwere ihe ọ pụtara n'asụsụ, nke a na-eji arụ okwu?
questions.explanation: A morpheme is the smallest meaningful unit in a language, used as a building block for constructing words.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị ahịrịokwu a na-akpọ 'ahịrịokwu mfe' (simple sentence)?
options: Ahịrịokwu nwere naanị otu echiche zuru oke
Ahịrịokwu nwere echiche abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa jikọtara ọnụ
questions.explanation: A simple sentence (ahịrịokwu mfe) expresses one complete idea, typically containing a single subject and verb.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị ahịrịokwu a na-akpọ 'ahịrịokwu mgbagwoju' (complex sentence)?
options: Ahịrịokwu nwere echiche abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa jikọtara ọnụ iji gosi echiche zuru oke
questions.explanation: A complex sentence (ahịrịokwu mgbagwoju) combines two or more clauses, often joined by a conjunction, to express a more elaborate idea.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọrụ ntụgharịasụsụ (translation) n'etiti Bekee na Igbo Izugbe?
options: Idepụta ahịrịokwu otu asụsụ ugboro abụọ
Mgbanwe echiche site n'otu asụsụ gaa n'ọzọ, na-echekwa isi ihe okwu ahụ pụtara
questions.explanation: Translation requires accurately conveying the meaning of a passage from one language to another, while preserving the original intended sense.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ngalaba ọmụmụ asụsụ nke na-elebara ọdịdị mkpụrụokwu na otu e si arụ ha (morphemes) anya?
questions.explanation: Morphology studies the internal structure of words, including roots, prefixes, and suffixes, and how they combine to form words.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ngalaba ọmụmụ asụsụ nke na-elebara otu e si edozi mkpụrụokwu iji rụọ ahịrịokwu nwere isi anya?
questions.explanation: Syntax examines how words are arranged and ordered to form grammatically correct and meaningful sentences.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu akụkụ ahịrịokwu Igbo na-egosi onye ma ọ bụ ihe ahịrịokwu na-ekwu maka ya?
options: Ihe a na-eme n'aha ya (Object) naanị
questions.explanation: The subject of a sentence identifies who or what the sentence is primarily about, typically performing the action of the verb.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mgbọrọgwụ ngwaa (verb root) tupu a tinye ntinye tensị ma ọ bụ ọnọdụ?
questions.explanation: The verb root is the base form of a verb before tense or aspect prefixes and suffixes are added to indicate timing or manner of action.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu akụkụ ahịrịokwu Igbo na-anata ihe omume ngwaa mere, dị ka onye ma ọ bụ ihe a na-eme ihe n'aha ya?
questions.explanation: The object of a sentence receives the action of the verb, as distinguished from the subject, which performs the action.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ntinye mkpụrụokwu n'ihu mgbọrọgwụ iji gbanwee ma ọ bụ gbasaa ihe ọ pụtara?
questions.explanation: A prefix is a morpheme attached to the beginning of a word's root, modifying or extending its meaning.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ntinye mkpụrụokwu n'azụ mgbọrọgwụ iji gbanwee ọrụ ma ọ bụ ihe ọ pụtara n'ahịrịokwu?
questions.explanation: A suffix is a morpheme attached to the end of a word's root, often changing its grammatical function within a sentence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'usoro adịgịị (gender) na ọnụọgụ (number) nke mkpọha Igbo, kedu ihe kpatara Igbo na-adabere karịsịa n'ọnọdụ okwu kama akara ngosi pụrụ iche?
options: Igbo nwere akara mgbanwe nsụpe zuru ezu maka nwoke na nwanyị
Mkpọha Igbo niile bụ nwoke naanị
Ọnụọgụ adịghị apụta ihe ma ọlị n'Igbo
Igbo anaghị egosipụta adịgịị na ọnụọgụ site na mgbanwe nsụpe ka Bekee, kama site n'okwu ndị ọzọ dị n'ahịrịokwu
questions.explanation: Unlike languages with grammatical gender endings, Igbo generally conveys gender and number distinctions through separate words or context rather than noun inflection.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọnụọgụ na-egosi na ihe a na-ekwu maka ya bụ naanị otu?
questions.explanation: Singular (otu) number refers to just one of the entity being discussed, contrasting with plural forms referring to more than one.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọnụọgụ na-egosi na ihe a na-ekwu maka ya karịrị otu?
questions.explanation: Plural (ọtụtụ) number indicates more than one of the entity in question, often marked in Igbo through separate plural markers or pronouns.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ahịrịokwu na-ajụ ajụjụ, dị ka 'Ị na-aga ebee?'
questions.explanation: An interrogative sentence is used to ask a question, distinct from declarative, imperative, or exclamatory sentence types.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ahịrịokwu na-enye iwu ma ọ bụ ntụziaka, dị ka 'Gaa n'ụlọ akwụkwọ!'?
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence gives a command or instruction, such as telling someone to go to school.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nyocha ahịrịokwu iji chọpụta akụkụ ya, dị ka onye/ihe na-eme ihe na ngwaa?
questions.explanation: Sentence parsing involves breaking down a sentence into its grammatical components to analyse its structure and function.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu na-egosi ọnọdụ ma ọ bụ àgwà nke mkpọha, dabere na otu ọ dị iche na ndịda ọzọ?
questions.explanation: Comparative adjective usage allows a speaker to compare the quality of one noun against another, an important grammatical function in descriptive sentences.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ederede a na-ede iji zipụ ozi n'ụzọ obodo ma ọ bụ nkeonwe, dị ka 'akwụkwọ ozi'?
questions.explanation: Letter writing (akwụkwọ ozi) covers both official and personal correspondence, following appropriate conventions for each type.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị akwụkwọ ozi a na-eziga ụlọ ọrụ ma ọ bụ ndị isi ọchịchị, nke na-eji usoro kwesịrị ekwesị?
questions.explanation: An official letter (akwụkwọ ozi ọrụ) is addressed to an institution, business, or authority, requiring a formal, structured tone.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị akwụkwọ ozi a na-eziga enyi ma ọ bụ ezinụlọ, nke na-eji olu ọmarịcha na-egosi mmekọrịta?
questions.explanation: A personal letter (akwụkwọ ozi nkeonwe) is written to a friend or family member, using a warm, familiar tone.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ederede na-egosi arụmụka iji kwado echiche mmadụ n'akụkụ ma ọ bụ n'akụkụ ọzọ?
questions.explanation: An argumentative composition (ruruka/arụmarụ) presents reasoned arguments to support or challenge a particular viewpoint on a debated topic.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ederede na-akọ akụkọ banyere ihe omume ma ọ bụ omenala, dị ka 'akụkọ'?
questions.explanation: A narrative composition (akụkọ) tells the story of specific events, experiences, or traditions in a structured, sequential form.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ole ka ọ dị ka ọnụ ọgụgụ okwu a na-achọ n'ime otu ederede WAEC Igbo?
questions.explanation: WAEC Igbo compositions are generally expected to be at least around 300 words to adequately develop the essay's topic.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ usoro mkpụrụ akwụkwọ Igbo a na-eji ede nsụpe ziri ezi, nke a na-akpọ 'Onwu Orthography'?
options: Usoro mkpụrụ akwụkwọ nke Onwu (Onwu Orthography guidelines)
questions.explanation: The Onwu Orthography establishes the standard spelling and writing conventions used for Standard Igbo today.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọrụ ịgụ ihe odide iji chọpụta isi ihe ndị dị n'ime ya?
questions.explanation: Comprehension (aghọtaịgbo) involves reading a passage to extract main ideas, analyse content, and understand the writer's message.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'aghọtaịgbo, gịnị ka a na-akpọ nyocha mkpụrụokwu dabere na otu e si eji ya n'ahịrịokwu?
options: Ịchọ okwu n'akwụkwọ ọkọwa okwu naanị
Nyocha okwu dabere n'ọnọdụ ya (contextual vocabulary analysis)
questions.explanation: Contextual vocabulary analysis involves interpreting a word's meaning based on how it is used within its surrounding sentence or passage.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Gịnị bụ nzọụkwụ mbụ dịkwesịrị ka nwa akwụkwọ mee tupu o bido ide ederede?
options: Ịhazi echiche na ịghọta isiokwu a ga-ede
questions.explanation: Before writing, it is important to plan and organise one's thoughts, ensuring a clear understanding of the topic to produce a coherent composition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ide akwụkwọ ozi ọrụ, gịnị kwesịrị ịpụta na mbido, tupu aha onye ga-anata ya?
options: Adreesị onye dere ozi na ụbọchị e dere ya
questions.explanation: A formal letter conventionally begins with the sender's address and the date, before the recipient's details and the body of the letter.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'akụkọ, gịnị ka a na-akpọ akụkụ na-emechi ihe niile mere n'akụkọ ahụ?
questions.explanation: The conclusion resolves the events and conflicts developed throughout the narrative, bringing the story to a satisfying end.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ederede ruruka, gịnị kwesịrị onye edemede ime iji kwado echiche ya?
options: Ide ahịrịokwu na-enweghị mmekọrịta na isiokwu
Inye ihe àmà na ihe atụ na-akwado echiche ya
Izere ikwu ihe àmà ọ bụla
questions.explanation: An effective argumentative essay provides supporting evidence and relevant examples to reinforce the writer's position on a topic.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nyocha e ji achọpụta ebumnobi onye edemede n'ime otu ederede?
questions.explanation: Analysing the author's intention involves considering the purpose behind the text and the message the writer aims to convey to readers.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'aghọtaịgbo, gịnị ka a na-akpọ isi echiche ma ọ bụ isiokwu bụ isi nke ederede ahụ na-akwado?
questions.explanation: The main idea or theme represents the central focus of a passage, the primary point the text seeks to communicate to the reader.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Gịnị kwesịrị nwa akwụkwọ ime mgbe o mechara ide ederede ya, tupu o were ya nye onye nchọpụta?
options: Ịgụghachi ya iji chọpụta mmejọ ụtọasụsụ na nsụpe
Ịkwafu ya n'ihe onye ọzọ dere
questions.explanation: Reviewing one's work before submission helps identify and correct grammatical errors and spelling mistakes, improving overall composition quality.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mkpụrụokwu ndị na-ejikọ echiche n'ụzọ ziri ezi n'ederede, dị ka 'nke mbụ', 'mgbe ahụ', 'n'ikpeazụ'?
questions.explanation: Connecting words like 'nke mbụ' (first), 'mgbe ahụ' (then), and 'n'ikpeazụ' (finally) help organise ideas logically within a composition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'akwụkwọ ozi nkeonwe, kedu ngalanye a na-eji amalite ozi ahụ n'ụzọ enyi na enyi?
options: Ekele ọnụ ala/mmasị (a warm, familiar greeting)
questions.explanation: Informal letters typically open with warm, familiar greetings, distinct from the formal openings used in official correspondence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọrụ a na-akpọ 'ịkọwa okwu dabere n'ihe gbara ya gburugburu' n'aghọtaịgbo?
options: Ịchọ okwu n'akwụkwọ ọkọwa okwu naanị
Nghọta okwu dabere n'ọnọdụ ya (contextual meaning interpretation)
questions.explanation: Interpreting contextual vocabulary involves understanding a word's meaning as it is used within its specific sentence or passage, rather than relying solely on a fixed definition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ederede bayani, gịnị dịkwesịrị ka onye edemede tinye iji mee ka ihe ọ na-akọwa pụta ìhè?
options: Kpọmkwem akụkọ metụtara mmetụta ahụ mmadụ, dị ka agba, ụda, na mmetụta anụ ahụ
questions.explanation: Effective descriptive writing uses vivid sensory details, such as colours, sounds, and feelings, to bring a scene or subject to life for the reader.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ emume a na-eme iji nye nwa ọhụrụ aha n'omenala Igbo?
questions.explanation: The naming ceremony (nkyalị) is a traditional Igbo rite performed to formally give a name to a newborn child.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ usoro nkwekọrịta di na nwunye n'omenala Igbo?
questions.explanation: Alụmdi na nwunye refers to the traditional Igbo marriage process and its associated customs and milestones.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ omenala e mere mgbe mmadụ nwụrụ, tupu e lie ya?
options: Olili na Akwamozu (funeral and burial rites)
questions.explanation: Olili na akwamozu describes the traditional funeral and burial customs observed following someone's death in Igbo culture.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ntinye aha ma ọ bụ nnata otuto n'omenala Igbo, dị ka ọzọ?
questions.explanation: Echichi (title-taking), such as the Ozo title, is a traditional honour bestowed on accomplished individuals within Igbo society.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu mmemme a na-eme iji nye ekele maka ihe ubi ọhụrụ, karịsịa ji, n'omenala Igbo?
questions.explanation: The New Yam Festival (Ịwa Ji Ọhụrụ) celebrates the harvest, giving thanks for the year's yam crop, a central agricultural festival in Igbo culture.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu egwuregwu a na-egwu n'abalị mgbe ọnwa na-acha, nke na-ababata ụmụaka na ndị okorobịa?
questions.explanation: Moonlight games (egwu ọnwa) are traditional evening play and storytelling activities held under the moonlight, often involving children and youths.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ihe ngosi mmụọ, nke na-egosipụta omenala na ntụkwasị obi Igbo?
questions.explanation: Masquerade displays (mmanwụ) are traditional performances featuring elaborately costumed figures representing spirits, deeply rooted in Igbo cultural practice.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu nkenke jupụtara n'amamihe, nke a na-eji ekwu ihe dị mkpa n'ụzọ dị nkenke?
questions.explanation: Proverbs (ilulu Igbo) are short, wisdom-laden sayings used to convey deep meaning and moral lessons concisely in Igbo speech.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu ma ọ bụ ụzọ e si eji ihe kwuo ihe ọzọ n'ụzọ atụmatụ, dị ka ntụnyere?
questions.explanation: Figures of speech (atụmatụ okwu) involve using language creatively, such as through comparison or exaggeration, to convey meaning beyond the literal.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ajụjụ egwuregwu jupụtara na nghọtahụ, nke ndị mmadụ na-agbalị ịchọpụta azịza ya?
questions.explanation: Riddles (gwa m gwa m) are traditional oral puzzles, often used for entertainment and to sharpen listeners' wit.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ agụmagụ e dere n'akwụkwọ, dị ka akụkọ mahụ mahụ na abụ?
questions.explanation: Written literature (agumagu ederede) refers to literary works recorded in writing, such as novels and poetry, unlike orally transmitted forms.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akwụkwọ akụkọ mahụ mahụ e dere n'ụdị proos, nke bụ otu n'ime ụdị agumagu ederede?
questions.explanation: A prose novel (ederede proos) is an extended narrative literary work, one of the major forms of written Igbo literature.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ederede e dere maka ime ihe ngosi n'elu ọnọdụ dram, ma ọ bụ fim?
questions.explanation: A play or dramatic script (ewumezewume) is written specifically for stage or screen performance.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nchịkọta abụ e dere n'ụdị agụmagụ nzuzo, nke bụ otu n'ime ụdị agumagu ederede Igbo?
questions.explanation: A poetry anthology (abu) is a compiled collection of written poems, following standardised poetic layouts within Igbo literature.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nzere ọ dị mkpa iji nyochaa akwụkwọ agụmagụ maka isiokwu ya, ihe odide, na usoro ya?
questions.explanation: Literary analysis involves closely examining a text's themes, characters, and structure to deepen understanding of the author's work.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'agumagu, kedu ihe a na-akpọ isi echiche ma ọ bụ ozi bụ isi nke onye edemede na-ebufe n'akwụkwọ ya?
questions.explanation: The theme (isiokwu) of a literary work is the central message or idea that the author conveys throughout the text.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'agumagu, kedu ihe a na-akpọ mmadụ nọ n'ime akụkọ, ya na àgwà ya na ọrụ ọ na-arụ n'akụkọ ahụ?
questions.explanation: A character (onye ọrụ) is a person portrayed within a literary work, defined by their traits, actions, and role in the story.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'agumagu, kedu ihe a na-akpọ ebe ma ọ bụ oge ihe omume akụkọ si mee?
questions.explanation: Setting refers to the time and place in which a story's events unfold.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'agumagu, kedu ihe a na-akpọ usoro pụrụ iche onye edemede ji ahọrọ okwu ma haziri ahịrịokwu ya?
questions.explanation: Style refers to an author's distinctive manner of using language, word choice, and sentence construction throughout their work.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọrụ ndị dabere n'omenala Igbo bụ 'ịkpa ǹkwụ' ma ọ bụ ọrụ e ji aka arụ n'ubi na ụlọ?
questions.explanation: Traditional Igbo occupations, such as farming, palm produce work, weaving, and crafts, form an important part of the region's cultural and economic history.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mmemme ndị a na-eme site n'obodo iji nabata ọhụụ ma ọ bụ ekele Chukwu maka ihe ubi?
questions.explanation: Community festivals, including harvest celebrations, are central social events in Igbo culture, expressing gratitude and communal unity.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nkwụkwarịrị ọha na eze n'omenala Igbo, ebe ndị okenye na-akwado ọchịchị obodo?
options: Nzuko ọha na eze/ndị okenye (council of elders)
questions.explanation: In traditional Igbo governance, councils of elders and titled community leaders typically play a central role in decision-making and dispute resolution.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọrụ mmadụ na-arụ n'ubi dịka isi ọrụ ndị Igbo?
questions.explanation: Farming (ọrụ ubi) has traditionally been a fundamental occupation and way of life for the Igbo people, central to their economy and festivals like Ịwa Ji.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nkwụkwarịrị e ji akpọ Ozo ma ọ bụ akpọ eze n'obodo Igbo?
questions.explanation: Title-taking systems, such as the Ozo title, confer social status and honour on accomplished individuals within Igbo communities.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ihe ọmụmụ gbasara ọdịnaala na omenala dị mkpa n'ọmụmụ asụsụ Igbo?
questions.explanation: Studying Omenala (culture and customs) alongside the language helps students understand the social practices and worldview of the Igbo people.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akụkọ ifo a na-akọ, nke jupụtara na mmụọ, anụmanụ na-ekwu okwu, na ihe ndị dị egwu?
questions.explanation: Folktales (akụkọ ifo) are traditional oral stories, often featuring spirits, talking animals, and other imaginative elements, passed down through generations.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ abụ ndị a na-agụ n'ọnụ, na-abụghị ndị e dere n'akwụkwọ, dị ka abụ nzuzo ma ọ bụ abụ mmemme?
questions.explanation: Oral poetry consists of ceremonial or historical verses traditionally performed aloud rather than composed in written form.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọdịnaala nke gosipụtara nsọpụrụ ọha na eze na-enye ndị okenye n'obodo Igbo?
questions.explanation: Deep respect for elders is a fundamental value embedded in Igbo culture, guiding social conduct and interactions within the community.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe kpatara ọ dị mkpa ịmụta Ilulu Igbo (proverbs) dị ka akụkụ nke agumagu Igbo?
options: Ha na-eburu amamihe na omume ọma nke a na-agbanyeere n'ụzọ dị nkenke ma doo anya
Ha bụ naanị maka ndị okenye
questions.explanation: Proverbs carry deep wisdom and moral guidance in a concise, memorable form, making them a valued part of Igbo oral literary tradition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nkwụkwarịrị ọha mmadụ n'obodo Igbo, ebe a na-egosipụta mmasọmasọ dị n'etiti ndị dere aha?
options: Ọtụtụ egwuregwu na ememe obodo (community sporting and festive events)
questions.explanation: Community sporting events and festivals bring together members of Igbo society, reinforcing communal bonds and cultural identity.
